how_to_use: Read this before calling set_plugin_param on Vital. It records which value FORMAT each parameter actually accepts, measured by setting and reading back. The tool docstring recommends the plugin's text form; for Vital that is wrong more often than it is right.

hosting_constraints.one_instance_per_plugin_name: Tracks that share the SAME plugin string share one instance and one patch, and a param change re-renders all of them. Use distinct path strings (see multiple_instances_via_path) when you need different sounds per track.
hosting_constraints.set_params_before_writing_clips: Each set_plugin_param re-renders all Vital tracks. Do patch design while those tracks have no clips (tracks_rerendered: 0) — it is effectively free then and slow afterwards.
hosting_constraints.editor_crash: Observed SIGSEGV in Vital's own GUI thread (SynthEditor::render(Canvas&) -> Renderer::run), which kills the whole app and any unsaved project. Triggered while a second client drove the same shared instance. Avoid driving Vital from two sessions at once, and prefer keeping its editor window closed during bulk clip writes.
hosting_constraints.multiple_instances_via_path: IMPORTANT: the one-patch-per-name limit is avoidable. load() keys _LOADED on the exact string you pass, and uses it directly when os.path.exists() is true. So passing distinct PATH strings yields independent instances, each with its own patch, and set_track accepts a path in 'plugin'. Verified with three simultaneous Vital patches: name 'Vital' (VST3), '/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components/Vital.component' (AU), and '/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/./Vital.vst3' (same VST3 binary, different key string). Any path variant that still resolves gives another instance. Each re-renders only ITS OWN tracks, so per-track patches also make param changes much cheaper.
hosting_constraints.au_build_returns_blank_display: The AU build ('...Vital.component') returns an empty 'value' string from set_plugin_param and plugin_params. Verify by 'raw' instead. The VST3 build returns proper display text.

au_cannot_be_snapshotted.symptom: save_plugin_preset on Vital.component returns 'plugin returned no state to save'; preset_bytes is empty. A track on the AU therefore saves with plugin_state = '' and LOSES ITS PATCH when the app restarts, silently -- the project file looks complete.
au_cannot_be_snapshotted.check: After saving, read the .fcp and confirm every track with a 'plugin' has a non-empty 'plugin_state'.
recovery: The AU will not give up preset_data, but it DOES report all 903 parameters. Both builds are the same Vital, with identical parameter keys.
1. plugin_params on the AU with query '' and limit 5000 -> 903 rows of raw values.

2. Check the 64 modulation_N_amount rows. If none differs from default, the patch    has no active routings, so the parameters ARE the whole patch and this    reconstruction is exact. If some are active, the routings cannot be recovered    this way -- they are not parameters.
3. In-process: load the VST3, restore vital_init, write every raw value on top,    then take preset_data and bank it. Doing this in one process avoids 903 bridge    round-trips.
4. load_plugin_preset onto a free path variant, then set_track(plugin=<that path>).
5. Verify: plugin_params on the new instance and diff all 903 raw values.
au_cannot_be_snapshotted.done_2026_08_25: Recovered the Digital Tiger bass this way. It turned out to be factory init plus 4 parameters (filter_1_cutoff 0.6, filter_1_resonance 0.3, oscillator_1_detune_power 0.65, oscillator_2_switch off) with no routings; all 903 matched after.
au_cannot_be_snapshotted.ordering_trap: _resync_plugin_tracks stamps state onto tracks whose 'plugin' ALREADY equals that name, so load_plugin_preset before set_track leaves plugin_state empty (the load reports tracks_rerendered: 0, which is the tell). Switch the track first, or load again after.
au_cannot_be_snapshotted.prefer: Use VST3 path variants for anything the agent will drive. The AU's only advantage is being another instance, and path variants give that too.

value_format_rules.default: Send a raw 0-1 float. Then READ THE RETURNED 'value' — set_plugin_param echoes what the plugin actually stored, so a wrong format is visible immediately.
value_format_rules.choice_and_switch: Use raw 1.0 / 0.0. Text names FAIL SILENTLY: sending 'On' set the switch to Off and still returned ok:true.
value_format_rules.percent_params: Send a FRACTION, not a percent string or a raw: 0.48 -> '48%'. The stored raw is sqrt(fraction), so 0.48 reads back as raw 0.6928. A 'NN%' string also works on the VST3 build and is REQUIRED for reverb_size.
value_format_rules.stepped_or_scaled: transpose, unison voices, tempo divisions and filter cutoff all need raw 0-1; their text forms were misparsed by large factors.
value_format_rules.time_params: reverb_decay_time misparsed BOTH forms. Set by trial and read back.
value_format_rules.envelope_times: Two observed behaviours. TEXT-parsed: value maps linearly to seconds over 0-32s, so send seconds/32. RAW: value is the 0-1 parameter and the curve is exponential — raw 0.02 -> 5us, 0.25 -> 0.125s, 0.30 -> 0.259s, 0.33 -> 0.379s, 0.36 -> 0.537s, 0.44 -> 1.2s, 0.67 -> 6.4s. Probe to find which one you are in.
value_format_rules.THE_BIG_CAVEAT: set_plugin_param's value handling depends on the LOADED PATCH, not just the parameter. envelope_1_decay took 0.0375 as text and gave 1.20s on the default patch; the identical call on Physical Tension was taken as RAW and gave 2 nanoseconds — silent. There is no way to know in advance. ALWAYS read back the echoed 'value', and probe two or three points before trusting a mapping.

envelope_and_time_law.solved_2026_08_25: Envelope/LFO times follow an exact 4th-power law, which is what made the earlier guesses look contradictory. seconds = (json_value)**4 for the field inside the preset JSON, and seconds = 32*(raw)**4 for the 0-1 parameter. So json_value = 2.3784 * raw.
envelope_and_time_law.practical: For a one-shot drum, sustain 1.0 and a release long enough that note-off does not truncate the sample. Release only matters up to the sample's own decay -- past that it changes nothing.

choice_params_in_json_are_indices.rule: A stepped/menu parameter is stored in the preset JSON as its INDEX, not as the 0-1 raw and not as the display string.
checks: lfo_1_sync json 1.0 = 'Tempo' (0 Seconds, 1 Tempo, 2 Tempo Dotted, 3 Tempo Triplets, 4 Keytrack)
choice_params_in_json_are_indices.how_to_enumerate: Load the plugin, walk raw_value over i/(num_steps-1) and read string_value; the index is i.

measured.note: raw 0.5 = 0 semitones; range is +/-48 over 97 steps
UNRELIABLE both ways. '2 secs' -> 64 secs; raw 0.62 -> 5e-05 secs. raw 0.5 = 1 sec, roughly exponential.

synthwave_supersaw.description: Wide detuned saw with a sub octave. Works as lead, arp and (an octave down) bass, which matters because all Vital tracks share one patch.

synthwave_bass.description: Tight sub-heavy bass. Put on its own instance via the AU path so it does not share the lead's patch.

synthwave_pad.description: Wide slow-swelling pad with an octave-up second osc. Needs its own instance because its 1.2s attack would ruin lead and bass.

percussion_kit.description: Four drum voices, one Vital instance each (a shared instance would force one patch on all of them). Preset choice verified against settings, not names.

kick.play_note: C4 / MIDI 60 — the patch transposes -27, sounding ~55 Hz
kick.handles: modulation_1_amount = lfo_1 -> osc_1_transpose (pitch-drop depth); modulation_3_amount = distortion drive

hats.note: same preset as the snare on a separate instance; only the envelope differs

synthesized_drum_oneshots.why: Vital's own percussion presets are tonal instruments with sustain envelopes; EQ cannot turn one into a drum. Synthesizing the sample and injecting it into the SMP slot gives an actual drum, and the patch around it is trivial.

shared_patch.env_1_release: 1.0 (= 1 s, longer than any of these samples)

recipes.anvil: Free-free bar modes at ratios 1 : 2.76 : 5.40 : 8.93 : 13.34 : 18.64 off f0=524 Hz, the 2.76 mode loudest, plus ~58 dense modes 700-13500 Hz, plus a 4 ms noise transient band-passed 1.8-10.5 kHz. Per-mode T60 falls with frequency. The inharmonic ratios are what stop it reading as a pitched pipe.
recipes.kick: Sine swept 134->46 Hz with a 28 ms time constant, amp decay 0.15 s, plus a 2nd harmonic at 0.22. Saturate the BODY only (tanh 1.7), then add the click -- saturating after burying it flattens the attack to nothing.
recipes.snare: Shell modes 186 + 331 Hz (decay 0.095 s), noise body 190-6500 Hz, buzz 2.4-10 kHz (decay 0.115 s), 8 ms click. Aim for roughly 16% low / 23% mid / 60% high band energy; all-sizzle reads as thin.
recipes.hat: The six 808 square frequencies 205.3, 304.4, 369.6, 522.7, 540, 800 Hz, high-passed at 6.8 kHz, decay 0.032 s, plus 30% noise.

synthesized_drum_oneshots.measured_balance_2026_08_25: Rendered offline at the mixer gains: kick 0 dB reference, snare -3.9 dB peak, hats -5.9, anvil -4.7. Judging by RMS alone is misleading for short sounds -- hats measured -32 dB RMS while sounding fine on peaks.

morphing_wavetable.goal: Add movement to a static patch without changing the sound it already has.
morphing_wavetable.method: FFT the existing keyframe-0 cycle, keep its phases, and build N frames by multiplying harmonic h by h**(tilt*f) for f = 0..1, plus a Gaussian formant bump that walks up the harmonic index. Normalize every frame to the ORIGINAL's RMS so morphing does not change level. Frame 0 is then identical to what was there, so modulation can only add richness.
morphing_wavetable.wiring: keyframes at position 0..255; component interpolation 1, interpolation_style 1. Route lfo_1 -> osc_N_wave_frame for slow movement (lfo_1_sync 1 'Tempo', tempo index 2-4 = 16/1..4/1, sync_type 1 'Sync' so voices move together) and velocity -> osc_N_wave_frame for touch.
morphing_wavetable.trap: Morph EVERY oscillator that is on. Morphing only osc_1 while osc_2 carried an equal level of plain Init wavetable moved the spectral centroid 1.5% -- inaudible. Morphing both moved it 18-44%.

preset_library.format: A .vital file is PLAIN JSON. Read it directly to learn a patch before or without loading it — settings.modulations lists every routing as {source, destination}, and its index+1 is the modulation_N_amount parameter that drives it. This is the only way to discover routings, since modulation source/destination are NOT exposed as parameters.
preset_library.picking_a_percussion_patch: Judge by settings, not name. A one-shot hit has env_1_sustain 0 with a short decay (Physical Tension: A=0 D=0.274 S=0 R=0). Sustain 1.0 means it drones and is not a drum. Velocity->osc_1_level and velocity->filter_1_cutoff routings mean ghost notes will actually read as softer and darker.
preset_library.double_pitch_tracking_trap: Some presets add a 'note -> osc_1_transpose' modulation ON TOP of osc_1_midi_track, which is already on. Pitch then tracks the keyboard TWICE and notes sound about an octave high and thin — heard as a squeak or ping when used for drums. Physical Tension does this at modulation_7_amount = 1.0, with filter_1_keytrack = 1.0 opening the filter as well. Fix: set that modulation amount to raw 0.5 (= amount 0) and filter_1_key_track to 0.5. ALWAYS scan a percussion preset's routings for a note->pitch destination before writing a part to it.

vstpreset_container.why: pedalboard.load_preset only accepts .vstpreset, and Vital's raw_state is an opaque 'VC3!' blob. But preset_data is a JUCE VST3 container that wraps the .vital JSON verbatim, so a preset can be built by swapping that JSON. fantasia_core.presets.splice_vital does this.

layout.[40:48]: int64 LITTLE-endian offset of the chunk list
layout.[48:224]: JUCE preamble: 'VstW' hdr, then a VST2 FXB header — 'CcnK' + int32 BIG-endian byteSize, 'FBCh', version, fxID 'Vita', fxVersion, numPrograms, future[128], then int32 BIG-endian chunkSize as the LAST 4 bytes
layout.[json_end:list_off]: 32 bytes of component-chunk padding, keep verbatim
layout.[list_off:]: 'List' + int32 count + per entry: 4-byte id, int64 offset, int64 size. Entries are ('Comp', 48, size) and ('Cont', list_off, 0).

five_fields_to_shift_by_delta: FXB 'CcnK' byteSize at preamble+4 after the magic — BIG-endian
FXB chunkSize, the last 4 bytes of the preamble — BIG-endian
vstpreset_container.failure_mode: Miss either BIG-endian field and restore_preset returns True while the plugin silently keeps its previous patch. Always verify by reading back a parameter the new patch changes (osc_1_transpose is a good probe).
vstpreset_container.sizes_seen: Kick Drum 1 175KB, Physical Tension 164KB, Metal Head 943KB. Padding-to-fit only works for patches smaller than the template; resizing the container handles any size.

parameter_catalog.what: All 903 parameters: key, display name, JSON field name, init value, raw value, type, steps, unit, group.
parameter_catalog.why_the_json_column_matters: 256 of the 903 have a DIFFERENT name inside the preset JSON than the name set_plugin_param takes. Writing the parameter name into the JSON adds a dead key the plugin ignores, and the real field keeps its old value -- no error. This cost a rendering: osc_1_on written as 'oscillator_1_switch' left the oscillator on and its saw drowned the sample under test.

capability_boundary.summary: Vital's PARAMETER surface is knobs only. It carries no wiring and no assets: there is no parameter for a modulation's source or destination, for which wavetable an oscillator holds, for which file is in the sample slot, or for an LFO's drawn shape. Through set_plugin_param alone, those four are UI-only.
capability_boundary.but_the_preset_json_carries_all_four: They live in the .vital JSON, which splice_vital rewrites into a loadable VST3 blob. All four were authored from scratch and verified against a live plugin -- so nothing in Vital is actually UI-only. The editor is a convenience, not a requirement.

verified_2026_08_25.modulation_routing: settings.modulations is a 64-entry list of {source, destination}; slot N maps to modulation_(N+1)_amount. Wrote {'source':'lfo_1','destination':'filter_1_cutoff'} into an empty slot 0; the plugin reported it back.
verified_2026_08_25.wavetable: settings.wavetables[osc].groups[0].components[0].keyframes[k].wave_data is base64 of 2048 float32 LE, range -1..1, one cycle. Generated a table of odd harmonics only; the render came back with partials at h1,3,5,7,9,11,13 and no even ones. Multiple keyframes at different 'position' values are what osc_N_wave_frame morphs through.
verified_2026_08_25.sample: settings.sample = {name, length, sample_rate, samples}, where samples is base64 of int16 LE MONO, exactly 'length' of them. Injected a 300 Hz sine; with sample_keytrack 0 it rendered at 300.0 Hz regardless of note played. This makes Vital a fully agent-drivable sampler.
verified_2026_08_25.lfo_shape: settings.lfos[N] = {name, num_points, points, powers, smooth}. points is a FLAT [x0,y0,x1,y1,...] list in 0..1, powers is one curve value per point (0 = linear). The stock Triangle is num_points 3, points [0,1, 0.5,0, 1,1]. Trivial to author -- no encoding involved.

still_genuinely_UI_only: Seeing and hearing the result -- the editor is the only visual feedback.
Vital's own preset browser metadata (tags, ratings) beyond author/name/style.
capability_boundary.init_patch_already_holds_white_noise: settings.sample is 'White Noise' (44100 int16) in the init patch with sample_on 0. A noise drum needs no file load at all -- just sample_on 1, sample_loop 0, sample_keytrack 0. This is how DT Snare and DT Hat were built.

steps: 3. edit patch['settings'] -- USE THE 'json' COLUMN of vital_params.json for names
5. presets.save('Vital', name, blob) then load_plugin_preset, OR set preset_data directly
json_authoring_recipe.always_verify: Snapshot the plugin back with save_plugin_preset and re-read the JSON. Both restore_preset and load_plugin_preset return ok/True on a blob the plugin then ignores; the readback is the only honest check. For audio, render and FFT.
json_authoring_recipe.instance_paths_are_not_free: A distinct path string is a distinct instance, but check list_tracks first -- '/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/./././././Vital.vst3' looked unused and was Vital Hats. Loading a test preset onto it overwrote the patch (the call even reported tracks_rerendered: 1, which is the tell).
